changelog: Data: the journal held only 17 of the Bitfunded Altcoin challenge's 58 real closed positions — everything logged from the point the app existed, a winner-weighted subset (+$773.83 at 62.5% win rate) of what Bitfunded's own Position History shows for the same challenge (-$195.32 across 58 at 39.7%). Migration 2026_09_17_0002 reconciles all 58: inserts the 41 missing rows and overwrites entry/exit price, time_in/time_out and pnl on the 17 existing rows with Bitfunded's own figures (the hand-typed originals differed by rounding). Also fixes two defects found during reconciliation: trade 59's trade_date was a stale 2026-08-17 against a 2026-08-13 time_in, and trade 77 was still marked Open though Bitfunded closed it 2026-09-05 for +$112.05

Schema: added trades.source ('manual'/'import', default 'manual') and trades.r_multiple_source ('recorded'/'estimated', NULL by default) — 2026_09_17_0001. Imported rows have no stop-loss price on file, so their R is reconstructed from observed full-size losses rather than a real stop distance; these columns let any statistic that presents R distinguish fact from estimate instead of quietly treating both the same

Data: R-multiple for the Bitfunded import is derived per-trade, not from the account's configured risk ladder — replaying the ladder against the observed position sizes shows it wasn't followed during the July/early-August drawdown (risk stayed near 1% while the ladder required 0.25%, a ~4x gap), so deriving from it would understate real losses by roughly that factor. Instead: a loss is treated as a full stop-out (r_multiple=-1.00, r_multiple_source='recorded') when 35<=|pnl|<=115, matching the convention already on the 17 pre-existing rows; every other trade gets r_multiple = pnl / (median |pnl| of nearby stop-outs, +/-7 days), r_multiple_source='estimated'. 29 of 58 rows land in each bucket — see the migration file and PR notes for the full risk_unit series

Fix: ReviewEngineController and StatsController now track what share of a scoped trade set has an estimated (not recorded) r_multiple, and the three review insights whose headline number is an R multiple (winrate/expectancy sanity check, period-trend comparison, aggressive-vs-reserved challenge comparison) append a caveat to their detail text when the underlying set is majority estimated — so a reconstructed R is never presented with the same confidence as a recorded one

Process: recorded two CLAUDE.md findings for future challenges — (1) a journal's trade count should be reconciled against the broker's own history before its statistics are trusted, since a partial subset can be silently winner-weighted; (2) the account's risk ladder was not followed during its drawdown, which the review engine should learn to detect by comparing risk_amount against the ladder tier implied by balance at entry
